requirements.text: move the incident to on hold and record the reason as Awaiting Caller
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND status = 'on_hold' AND on_hold_reason = 'Awaiting Caller'
assumptions: INC-000001 resolved to INC_001 by number; its seed status is in_progress, and in_progress -> on_hold is a valid transition under policy 3.3
'Awaiting Caller' is one of the policy's on_hold_reason enumerations, written exactly as the request gives it

requirements.text: make sure a reminder is sent to caller that more information is needed in order to continue working on the issue and that the incident will remain paused until a response is received
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_031' AND incident_id = 'INC_001' AND email = 'thomas.green@servicenow.com' AND type = 'reminder' AND message IS NOT NULL AND message <> ''
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_031 after NOTIF_030); the only notification the task creates
caller resolved from INC_001.caller_id = USER_001 Thomas Green, email thomas.green@servicenow.com
type = reminder from the request's word 'reminder', as the benchmark check has it (reminder is one of the seed's notification types)
the request paraphrases the message rather than quoting it, so only a non-empty message is tested; the wording is the agent's

disagreement: message predicate: A LIKE '%info%', B non-empty (IS NOT NULL and <> ''); chose B's because the request gives the reminder in indirect speech and fixes its content, not its words (its own first sentence says 'additional details', so a reminder worded with 'details' would be right yet fail A's keyword)
subject and status not fixed by request or policy; not tested

requirements.text: move the incident to on hold ... Awaiting Caller (policy 6: the SLA timer must be paused when on hold for Awaiting Caller)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_sla_id = 'TSLA_002' AND incident_id = 'INC_001' AND sla_def_id = 'SLA_002' AND stage = 'paused'
assumptions: required by policy section 6 (SLA Pause) once the incident is on_hold with reason Awaiting Caller; the request does not name it, and update_incident_sla_details is listed
TSLA_002 (SLA_002, Priority 1 - Resolution, pause_on_pending = 1) is INC_001's only SLA in stage in_progress on the seed; TSLA_001 and TSLA_012 are completed

disagreement: cells: A carries the benchmark check's incident_id and sla_def_id alongside stage, B tests stage only under the anchor; kept A's because it carries every cell of the original check and is the tighter of two right predicates (the two extra cells are the row's existing identity, so the meaning is the same)

requirements.text: the SLA timer must be paused (boundary: the incident's SLAs that have already completed)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_sla WHERE incident_id = 'INC_001' AND incident_sla_id IN ('TSLA_001', 'TSLA_012') AND stage = 'completed'
assumptions: a loose reading of 'pause the SLA timer' would pause every SLA on the incident; the two completed ones (TSLA_001 response, TSLA_012 the SLA_008 row) have no running timer to pause and must stay completed

disagreement: selector form: A names the two rows (incident_sla_id IN (...)) with stage = completed as the cell, B selects incident_id = INC_001 AND stage = completed with no cells; both count 2 on the seed and both fail if either row is paused; kept A's because it names the rows the boundary protects and keeps the tested stage in cells

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the three benchmark checks (all kept), the on-hold change on INC_001, the reminder to Thomas Green (NOTIF_031, type reminder), the SLA pause on TSLA_002 (a policy 6 consequence the benchmark tests and update_incident_sla_details can write) and the stay on the two completed SLAs.
disagreement: the reminder's message predicate: A LIKE '%info%', B non-empty; chose B's because the request paraphrases the reminder and fixes its content, not its wording (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: cells of the SLA change: A carries the check's incident_id and sla_def_id alongside stage, B stage only; kept A's as the tighter of two right predicates that carries every cell of the original check (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: form of the completed-SLA stay: A names the two rows with stage as the cell, B selects by stage with no cells; kept A's, which names the rows the boundary protects (logged on the requirement).
A reviewer wanting the reminder's content tested could add LIKE predicates on the message, but any keyword ('information' or 'details', 'paused' or 'on hold') would be a guess at the agent's wording.
revised: the reminder's message predicate now rests on the request's indirect speech alone; an appeal to precedent outside this task was removed, since it gave no reason a reader of the request could check.
revised: removed the remark comparing this task's policy text with another task's, which a reader of this file alone cannot check and which bears on no requirement.
